title: Finite Tor dimension on affine opens of a relatively flat proper image
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be proper, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, and $F$ a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $f$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Supply independent derived localizations on $X$ and $S$ [def-pc-derived-category]. For any affine open $U\subseteq S$ with a derived localization in the target morphism universe, the exact open restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps] of $Rf_*(F[0])$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] has finite Tor dimension on $U$ [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension]: one interval $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$ bounds its derived tensor cohomology with every $\mathcal O_U$-module. Bounds may vary with $U$. No pseudo-coherence, finite-free representative or perfection is asserted.

proof.text: On the supplied affine U, use quasi-compactness and compactness of U to make its inverse image Y compact. Reindex the finite subcover of Y.affineCover by Fin r. Properness supplies separatedness of f restricted to U. Restrict relative flatness using the proved private flatOver_openImmersion_square helper: for any commutative square with open immersions on source and base, transport section flatness along the base section-ring isomorphism and identify the scalar action using appLE_comp_appLE. Apply it to the restriction square using morphismRestrict_ι. No pullback hypothesis is needed in the helper. Form P = finiteAffineCechModel (f restricted to U) (F restricted to Y) V. finiteAffineCechModel_ge and finiteAffineCechModel_le give termwise vanishing outside [0,r]; finiteAffineCechModel_flatOver gives flatness over the identity.

Supply the standard derived localization on Y; keep the supplied independent localizations on X, S and U. finiteAffineCechModel_derivedComparison gives Q(P) isomorphic to the direct image of the restricted module in degree zero. mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor and overFunctorEquiv identify exact restriction of F[0] with the single complex of the restricted module. Compose the inverse of this comparison under the restricted direct image with the inverse component of schemeDerivedDirectImage_openRestriction. This gives Q(P) isomorphic to the requested restriction of Rf_*(F[0]).

Apply isFlat_of_affineFlatOver_identity to each term of P, then isKFlat_of_boundedAbove_flat_ringedSpace with upper bound r. For any test module M and integer n outside [0,r], mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso identifies the total tensor P tensor M[0] with termwise tensor by M. tensorRight M preserves the zero degree-n term. The homology short complex therefore has zero middle object, so isZero_homology_of_isZero_X₂ gives zero homology. Use witnesses 0,r with 0 ≤ r in HasFiniteTorDimension, and use P, its K-flatness, and the composed representing isomorphism in schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes. The proof does not require a nonempty cover, a nonzero coefficient module, or a nonempty base.

theorem properFlat_single_local_hasFiniteTorDimension
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wS}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace))]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] (hF : F.IsFlatOver f)
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wS}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))] :
    U.toScheme.HasFiniteTorDimension ((schemeOpenRestriction S U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
      ((schemeDerivedDirectImage f).obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj F)))
